params.body:
Closes the finding `de-website-toont-enkel-gepubliceerde-onverkochte-wagens` (R S2-5.2, one of the disputed rules).

A dealer's website has two doors onto the same stock: the iframe embed and the public API. The API asked for `is_complete`, the embed did not. A vehicle the dealer was still filling in, with the website tick already on, was therefore public in the iframe and absent from the API.

What makes this the kind of difference that survives for months: `PublicVehicleController::baseQuery` carries the comment *"Same scope as the website embed's own-stock branch: published, unsold, complete vehicles of this dealer."* It was written down as true, so nobody checked it.

`is_complete` now sits with the other three conditions in `forWebsiteQuery`, which both doors read. They no longer each know their own version of the rule, and the API's comment is now accurate.

**Measured on production before changing anything**: 1719 own vehicles with the website tick, of which 24 incomplete, of which 5 unsold, across 4 dealers. Those 5 disappear from the iframe. They were never in the API, and they are sheets their dealer had not finished: a car with missing fields, published by a tick on a form still being filled in rather than by a decision.

`TheEmbedAndTheApiAgreeOnDraftsTest` puts the two doors side by side instead of testing each alone, with the boundary that the tick is still what publishes. Verified to bite: without the condition the first test fails.

R S2-5.2 moves from `betwist` to `code`; disputed rules go from 37 to 36. Full suite green, PHPStan clean.
params.title: The embed and the API agree on drafts
